# libsrtp / srtp-fuzzer

libsrtp's own fuzz target `srtp-fuzzer` ([source](source/fuzzer.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over libsrtp (cisco/libsrtp at 2cb11879).

Builds an SRTP session from input-derived policies (profile, SSRC, keys, MKIs, header-extension ids, window), adds/removes streams, sets and gets ROCs, then repeatedly runs an input-chosen protect/unprotect (RTP or RTCP) and a second input-chosen operation on the result. Status codes only steer control flow; protect->unprotect output is never compared with the original packet, and the ROC read back after srtp_stream_set_roc is not compared with the value set.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against libsrtp at commit 2cb11879.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- abort() if an SRTP profile's master key + salt length exceeds SRTP_MAX_KEY_LEN ("Shouldn't happen for a public profile") -- a check over the library's fixed profile table, trivially true ([lines 382-387](source/fuzzer.c#L382-L387)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libsrtp` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `srtp-fuzzer.plain` | 327,712 | `0900c0bdd261144f258acbb5b1a33fbc8942df9391ebb4b777b43f3130fc1bab` |
| ubsan | `srtp-fuzzer.ubsan` | 338,152 | `4d5d18e1318de3865b7a07cbc85980d783b4408b9d75f2f76ed4a4765c279884` |
| asan | `srtp-fuzzer.asan` | 942,104 | `1a0cf0c42da0dab916c9c2875eea424008eb0b9fd647135502104fcc1d0d2ab3` |
| asan-ubsan | `srtp-fuzzer.asan-ubsan` | 931,640 | `a8624c30787e774902dcc5621e8efc572686876649ff94b20e75f5ac09794f23` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
